data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's bulk-discount counterfactual and SRC_005's linear-rate answer share a mechanism: both treat the per-pencil price as a function of quantity, differing only in the sign of the derivative (negative for discounts, zero for uniform). The two positions are compatible under a general pricing-function framework; they are refuted if a pricing model exists in which the per-pencil price is not a monotonic or constant function of quantity (e.g., oscillating or discontinuous tier schedules), which would break both the bulk-discount narrative and the uniform-rate narrative simultaneously.
